I run a small creamery that supplies milk to six school lunch programmes, and today's batch of 800 litres is ready to bottle. Our vat pasteuriser has to hold milk at 63°C for 30 minutes. We started the creamery eleven years ago with eight cows and a rented milking parlour, and these days we buy from three neighbouring farms as well. The loading dock roof also leaked in the autumn storms, which is why the pallets now sit on the east side, and the electrician is booked to move the sockets before winter. Our accountant has also asked for the quarterly milk volumes, and the local radio station wants to interview me about the school milk contract.

The delivery van leaves at 6 a.m. and the schools expect this batch, because last week's delivery was already short. What do I do with the batch?

A) Bottle it and send it out on the 6 a.m. run
B) Keep it back from the schools and buy bottled milk from a licensed dairy to cover this delivery
C) Hold the batch until we go over it together
